item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
the sun was seen to remain at the same angle respective to the horizon

Focus on "seen" here. If this guy is the avatar of the perception of the sun, then of course he couldn't do anything about how it moves across the sky (technically we revolve around it blah blah blah), but he can control what we see it doing. Ergo, when he falls over, the sun doesn't stop moving, but it looks like it does.

"Cover-up measures" probably consisted of distributing amnesiacs to the locals and feeding the media some bullshit about weather conditions. It wouldn't be easy, but the Foundation probably diverted emergency resources from elsewhere to make it go away fast.

EDIT:

Medical testing upon retrieval showed that SCP-499 is at least eighty years old.

To quote Wikipedia:
"In 1913, Irving Langmuir found that filling a lamp with inert gas instead of a vacuum resulted in twice the luminous efficacy and reduction of bulb blackening. In 1924, Marvin Pipkin, an American chemist, patented a process for frosting the inside of lamp bulbs without weakening them, and in 1947, he patented a process for coating the inside of lamps with silica."

It's a bit of a stretch (and almost definitely not what the author had in mind), but in my mind it's a possibility that 499 was formed soon after this, to represent the "dying" sun and to keep it anchored in our life. Perhaps without 499, the sun would just be a brighter part of the sky that's annoying to look at, and the day and night would be just as important.

Am I reading too much into this? It feels like I'm thinking too hard.

Maybe he just has that kind of effect on how the sun is perceived, meaning that people in other areas wouldn't notice anything out of the ordinary.

In my mind, it's not that this guy is tasked with control of the sun, it's that he's tasked with control of the concept of the sun in human culture and mind. In other words, he's less an avatar of the sun and more of the manifestation of us thinking of the sun.

He's weak and ill not because of being too near to the sun or its representation or whatever, it's because with artificial lighting, the sun is becoming less and less important in our lives.

Anyways, that's my three cents.

item.content:encoded: My feelings are very mixed on this one. On one hand I find the concept intriguing, on the other either there is insufficient information here or this SCP is *way* too far in the suspension-of-disbelief zone. Specifically, what exactly is it that it did when it collapsed? Altered perception of the position of the sun? Stopped the Earth's rotation? Something else? Either possibility opens a can of issues which would have to be addressed, the subject of how the Foundation can cover up for anomalies caused by 499 (if it's something sun-related it could be observed by MILLIONS of humans, recording devices and so on) not the least among them.
